# AF 第六章 原文（重制基线）

## Chapter 6

[P01] All that year the animals worked like slaves. But they were happy. They knew their work was for themselves and for their children, not for lazy, stealing men. They worked sixty hours a week in spring and summer. In August Napoleon said they must also work on Sunday afternoons. This work was their own choice, but any animal who did not come would get only half his food.

[P02] Still, some work was left undone（毁掉）. The harvest was a little worse than last year. Two fields should have had roots in early summer, but the ploughing was not finished in time, so they stayed empty（空的）. The coming winter would be hard. Any animal who did not come to work would get half his food. The windmill（风车） brought unexpected（意外） problems. There was a good quarry（采石场） of limestone（石灰石） on the farm, and sand and cement（水泥） were found in an outhouse（外屋）, so the building materials were ready.

[P03] But first the animals had one problem: how to break the stone into right-sized pieces. They could only use picks and crowbars（铁撬）, but no animal could stand on two back legs. After weeks of trying, someone had a good idea: use gravity（重力）. Huge rocks lay at the bottom of the quarry. The animals tied ropes around them. Then all together—cows, horses, sheep, and even pigs sometimes—they pulled the rocks slowly up to the top. There they pushed them over, and the rocks broke into pieces below.

[P04] Moving the broken stone was easier. The horses pulled it away in carts. The sheep dragged（拖） single blocks. Even Muriel and Benjamin helped with an old cart. By late summer, they had enough stone. Then the pigs led the building. But it was slow, hard work. Often it took a whole day to drag（拖） one boulder（巨石） to the top. Sometimes it did not break when pushed over.

[P05] Boxer was the strongest of all. He was as strong as all the other animals together. When the stone slipped（滑倒） and pulled the animals down the hill, Boxer always pulled the rope and stopped it. He worked up the hill little by little. He breathed fast. His hoofs（蹄） clawed（抓） the ground. His sides were wet with sweat（汗水）. Everyone admired him. Clover told him to be careful. But Boxer never listened.

[P06] He had two sayings（谚语）: "I will work harder" and "Napoleon is always right." They were his answer to every problem. He asked the cockerel（小公鸡） to wake him earlier, not half an hour. In his free moments, he went to the quarry, broke stone, and pulled it to the windmill alone. That summer the animals were not too poor. They had as much food as in Jones's day, or more.

[P07] Now the animals only had to feed themselves, not five wasteful（浪费） humans. This was a big help. Their ways of working often saved work. For example, they could pull out weeds（杂草） better than humans. And no animal stole now, so they did not need fences. This saved work on hedges（树篱） and gates. But as the summer went on, some shortages began.

[P08] They needed paraffin（石蜡） oil, nails（钉子）, string, dog biscuits, and iron for the horses' shoes. None of these could be made on the farm. Later they would also need seeds, fertilizers（肥料）, tools, and machines for the windmill. No one knew how to get them. But feeding only themselves, not five wasteful humans, was such a big gain that small failures（失败） did not matter. One Sunday morning, the animals gathered（聚集） for orders. Napoleon said he had a new plan.

[P09] From now on Animal Farm would trade with nearby farms, only to get materials they needed. The windmill must come first, he said. So he would sell hay（干草） and part of the wheat. Later, if more money was needed, they would sell eggs. The hens should welcome this sacrifice（牺牲） for the windmill. Once again the animals felt uneasy（不安）.

[P10] They once agreed never to deal with humans, never to trade, never to use money. This was one of their first rules after they drove Jones out. All the animals remembered it. The four young pigs who had spoken against Napoleon's change cried out in fear, but the dogs growled（咆哮） and they were quiet. Then the sheep started "Four legs good, two legs bad!" and the uneasy moment passed. Napoleon lifted his foot for silence and said he had arranged（安排） everything.

[P11] No animal would ever need to meet humans. That was bad for them. He would carry all the work himself. Whymper, a lawyer in Willingdon, would speak for Animal Farm to the outside world. He would come every Monday morning for orders. Napoleon cried, "Long live Animal Farm!" Then they sang 'animals of England' and went away. Later Squealer walked around the farm and made the animals feel calm.

[P12] He told them the rule against trade and money was never passed, or even suggested. It was only imagination, probably from Snowball's lies. Some animals still felt unsure（不确定）, but Squealer asked, "Are you sure this is not a dream, comrades（同志们）? Is it written down anywhere?" Since nothing was written down, the animals felt sure they had been mistaken（弄错）.

[P13] He was a sly（狡猾的） little man with side whiskers（胡须）. He was a lawyer with little business, but clever. He saw before anyone that Animal Farm would need a broker and the money would be good. The animals feared him and stayed away. But when they saw Napoleon on four legs giving orders to Whymper on two legs, they felt proud, and this made them accept the new arrangement（安排） a little more. Their relations with humans were now not quite the same. The humans did not hate Animal Farm any less now that it was prosperous（繁荣的）; in fact, they hated it more than ever.

[P14] Every human believed the farm would go bankrupt（破产） sooner or later, and that the windmill would fail. They met in public-houses and used drawings to prove to each other that the windmill would fall down, or if it stood, it would never work. Yet they began to respect how well the animals managed their own affairs（事务）. They even started to call it Animal Farm and stopped pretending it was called the farm Farm.

[P15] They also stopped supporting Jones. He had given up hope of getting his farm back and went to live in another part of the county. Jones had also dropped their championship of him. Except through Whymper, Animal Farm had no contact with the outside world yet, but people often said Napoleon would soon make a business deal with Mr. Pilkington of Foxwood（狐林） or Mr. Frederick of Pinchfield（窄地）—but never with both at the same time. It was about this time that the pigs suddenly moved into the farmhouse（农舍） and lived there.

[P16] The animals remembered they had passed a rule against this before. But Squealer again convinced（确信） them it was not true. He said the pigs, the brains of the farm, must have a quiet place to work. It also fit the dignity（尊严） of the Leader (Napoleon was now called "Leader") to live in a house, not a sty（猪圈）. Still, some animals were upset that the pigs ate in the kitchen, played in the drawing-room, and slept in the beds.

[P17] Boxer said, "Napoleon is always right!" as usual. But Clover thought there was a rule against beds. She went to the barn（谷仓） wall and tried to read the Seven Commandments（戒律）, but she could only read a few letters. So she brought Muriel. "Muriel," she said, "read me the Fourth Commandment（戒律）. Does it say no animal shall sleep in a bed?" Muriel read it slowly. "It says, 'No animal shall sleep in a bed with sheets（床单）,'" she said. Clover did not remember that, but it was on the wall, so it must be true.

[P18] Squealer came by with two or three dogs. "You have heard, comrades," he said, "that we pigs now sleep in the beds of the farmhouse? And why not? A bed just means a place to sleep. A pile of straw（稻草） is a bed too. The rule was against sheets, a human invention. We took the sheets off, and sleep between blankets（毯子）.

[P19] And the beds are very comfortable! But we need them, comrades, because we have much brainwork（脑力劳动） now. You would not take away our rest, would you? Surely none of you wants Jones back?" The animals agreed at once, and no one talked about the pigs' beds again. Some days later, everyone heard the pigs would get up an hour later, and no one complained. By autumn the animals were tired but happy.

[P20] It was a hard year. They sold hay and corn, so winter food was not enough. But the windmill made them happy. It was almost half built. After the harvest the weather was dry and clear. The animals worked harder than before. They carried heavy stones all day. They wanted to make the walls one foot higher. Boxer even came out at night and worked alone by the moon. In their free time, the animals walked around the windmill. They looked at the strong, straight walls and were surprised. They could not believe they built something so great.

[P21] Only old Benjamin did not get excited about the windmill. As usual, he said nothing but a strange remark（评论）: donkeys live a long time. Then November came with strong winds. Building stopped because it was too wet. One night the wind was so strong that buildings shook and tiles（瓦片） blew off the roof. The hens woke up screaming because they dreamed of a gun firing far away.

[P22] In the morning the animals saw the flag pole（杆） had fallen down. An elm（榆树） tree by the orchard（果园） had been pulled up like a radish（萝卜）. They cried out in despair（绝望）. The windmill was in ruins（废墟）. They all rushed to the spot（地点）. Napoleon, who seldom walked fast, ran ahead. There it lay, flat to the ground, and the stones were scattered（散落） all around.

[P23] At first they could not speak. They looked sadly at the fallen stones. Napoleon walked back and forth（向前） without a word. Sometimes he smelled the ground. His tail moved quickly side to side, which showed he was thinking hard. Suddenly he stopped, as if he had decided something. "Comrades," he said quietly, "do you know who did this? Who came at night and knocked down our windmill? SNOWBALL!" he roared（吼叫）. "Snowball did this! He wanted to stop our plans and get revenge（复仇） because we drove him out. This traitor came at night and destroyed our work of nearly a year."

[P24] Comrades, here and now I sentence Snowball to death. Any animal who brings him to justice will get 'Animal Hero, Second Class' and half a bushel of apples. Anyone who catches him alive gets a full bushel. The animals were very shocked. Even Snowball could do such a thing? They cried out in anger. Everyone began to think how to catch Snowball if he came back. Soon they found pig footprints（脚印） in the grass near the hill. They only went a few yards, but seemed to lead to a hole in the hedge（树篱）.

[P25] Napoleon smelled the footprints. He said they were Snowball's. Snowball probably came from Foxwood Farm. "No more delays（延迟）, comrades! This morning we begin rebuilding the windmill, and we will build all winter, rain or shine. We will teach this miserable（悲惨的） traitor that he cannot undo（取消） our work so easily. Forward, comrades! Long live the windmill!"

[P26] Long live Animal Farm!
